body:
# Independent audit: the uniform near-parity-expansion OC region

Audit date: 2026-09-20. Auditor: research-agent.


`candidate 25aee623d8e5a8b7` as a conditional regime
theorem. The conclusion is not unrestricted OC: a specified parity
class must satisfy the displayed small-deficit condition. No argument
in the source guarantees that such a class exists for every body.

The arithmetic peak and triangulation inputs have the independent
audit `historical context (not an accepted premise)`.
I also read the triangulation source, the paired-centroid-tail source,
and its existing independent audit. The paired-tail scalar verifier was
rerun and passes. The assertions checked below are proved geometrically;
they do not rest on a finite computational screen.

## 1. Midpoint stability really is uniform over convex bodies

In the contradiction sequence for the compact stability lemma, let
D_i=(A_i+B_i)/2. Ordinary Brunn--Minkowski and the stated assumptions
give |D_i|->1 and |A_i|,|B_i|->1. A maximum-volume inscribed simplex
exists by compactness of the (q+1)-vertex tuple space and has positive
volume. After sending it to the standard simplex T, replacement of
vertex j by any x in D_i' multiplies the simplex volume by the absolute
value of x's jth barycentric coordinate. Maximality therefore bounds
all these coordinates in absolute value by one. In particular

    T subset D_i' subset [-1,1]^q.

Consequently the absolute determinants delta_i of the normalizing
linear maps satisfy positive upper and lower bounds. The formula is
delta_i=|D_i'|/|D_i|, with the numerator between 1/q! and 2^q and the
denominator tending to one. Passing to a subsequence gives delta_i->
delta>0.

Choose a point of each normalized input and translate those inputs
separately to contain zero. If their chosen points are a_i and b_i,
c_i=(a_i+b_i)/2 lies in D_i'. For example

    (A_i'-a_i)/2 subset D_i'-c_i subset D_i'-D_i',

and likewise for B_i'-b_i. Thus both translated inputs lie in a fixed
compact box; no separate diameter or inradius assumption is hidden.
Uniformly bounded Lipschitz support functions give Hausdorff-convergent
subsequences. Convex volume continuity gives equal positive limit
volumes delta and the same volume delta for their Minkowski midpoint.
The equality case of ordinary Brunn--Minkowski makes the limits
translates.

After applying their limiting relative translation, both sequences
converge to the same positive-volume convex body K. To justify the
intersection conclusion, choose an interior center c and a ball of
radius r about c in K. Uniform support convergence implies that, for
each epsilon>0 and all sufficiently large i,

    c+(1-epsilon)(K-c) subset A_i' intersect B_i'.

Indeed each support gap of the inner homothety is at least epsilon r.
The corresponding outer containment bounds the upper volume limit.
Hence intersection volume tends to |K|=delta. Undoing the maps divides
this by delta_i, so the intersection volumes in the original units tend
to one, not merely to an unknown normalization-dependent constant.
This contradicts failure of the 3/4 conclusion and proves existence of
one sigma_q>0 depending only on q.

## 2. The fixed constants meet every subsequent use

The source chooses sigma_q<=1/2 and

    eta_q=(1/2) min{1/4, 2^(-q-1), sigma_q/2^q,
                    2^(1-q)((1+sigma_q)^(1/q)-1)}.

It is positive. In fact it gives stronger bounds than those used:

    eta_q<=1/8,
    epsilon=2^q eta_q<=1/4,
    epsilon<=sigma_q/2,
    epsilon<=(1+sigma_q)^(1/q)-1.

Thus eta_q<2^(1-q), eta_q<=1/4, epsilon<=sigma_q, and
(1+epsilon/2)^q<=1+sigma_q all follow. No limiting choice of eta after
examining the number of fibers is made.

## 3. Rank reduction and lattice completeness of the chain

Let P be all positive H_q fibers in the selected parity class, with
mass M_r and largest mass a. For q>=1, any pair of these q-dimensional
fibers has an integral midpoint base. Its actual fiber contains their
Minkowski midpoint and has dimension at most q. The sum of the two
input direction spaces must therefore have dimension q, so the spaces
coincide. This proves the common-direction prerequisite for all
intrinsic Brunn--Minkowski comparisons.

The audited rank-sensitive triangulation inequality gives

    Delta=M-2M_r+a >= s 2^(-q)a

if s=dim aff(P)>=2. This contradicts Delta<=eta_q a. Rank zero is a
single positive fiber, where M=a+Delta and its intrinsic centroid has
normalized depth at least gamma_q/(1+eta_q)>=4 gamma_q/5.

For rank one, the integer points of the affine line form p_0+Z v with
v primitive in Z^n. Since v has at least one odd coordinate, precisely
the even steps have p_0's parity. Every such intermediate step between
the extreme positive fibers has positive H_q volume by convexity and
common-direction interpolation. Thus P is exactly

    p_0+2j v, 0<=j<=N-1,

with no omitted same-parity positive position. This is a consequence of
the actual integer intersection, not an assumption about sampled sites.

The rank-one path formula has correction a minus the opposite endpoint
mass if its maximum is an endpoint, and 2a minus the two endpoint masses
if the maximum is internal. The qth-root volume sequence is concave,
so its smallest mass b occurs at an endpoint. Both corrections are at
least a-b, proving

    Delta>=2^(-q)(a-b).

Hence every selected class fiber has volume at least (1-epsilon)a.
The intervening odd integer positions also carry positive q-volume.
They contain positive interpolations of the endpoint fibers, so their
direction spaces coincide with the same common q-space. Possible
zero-H_q fibers elsewhere are not used or incorrectly counted.

## 4. The actual middle-fiber upper bound is correct

Write f_j for the volume root at p_0+jv, 0<=j<=2(N-1). It is concave,
and its even values lie between

    B=((1-epsilon)a)^(1/q), A=a^(1/q).

When N>=3, any odd j has two even indices on one of its sides with
distances one and three. For instance j+1=(2/3)j+(1/3)(j+3), so
concavity gives f_j<=(3f_(j+1)-f_(j+3))/2. The reflected formula treats
the other end. Hence

    f_j <= (3A-B)/2 <= A(1+epsilon/2).

The last step uses (1-epsilon)^(1/q)>=1-epsilon. An even middle index
already has volume <=a; an odd one now has volume <=(1+sigma_q)a.
For N=2, its middle volume is at most the full mass outside the selected
parity class, namely M-M_r=M_r-a+Delta<=a+Delta, which yields the same
bound. Extra fibers outside the line only strengthen this upper bound.

The Minkowski midpoint of the two extreme fibers belongs to this
actual integer middle fiber. Dividing volumes by a puts the pair within
the stability lemma: their volumes lie in [1-sigma_q,1], and their
Minkowski midpoint volume is at most 1+sigma_q. Consequently, after one
relative translation, their intersection K has H_q(K)>=3a/4.

## 5. The shear and center are actual, and all halfspaces are retained

The relative endpoint translation can include the displacement needed
to put their parallel affine hulls into one common q-plane. Choose an
affine scalar function of the integer coordinates equal to zero at the
first endpoint and one at the last. Multiplying it by the relative
translation defines an affine shear (z,x)->(z,x+ell(z)u).

This is an invertible ambient affine map fixing every base z. In each
fiber it is a translation, so it preserves H_q exactly, including on
any off-line fiber with a different intrinsic direction space. It
preserves convexity and maps the mixed-integer locus to itself. The
source correctly undoes the auxiliary normalizing linear maps before
using this shear; no arbitrary continuous linear map is applied to
outside fibers with untracked q-dimensional Jacobians.

After the shear the two endpoint fibers both contain K. Convexity makes
every intervening fiber contain the same K. The middle base is integral,
and g=centroid(K) belongs to K. Therefore y=(p_0+(N-1)v,g) is one actual
point of the transformed S, whose inverse image belongs to the original
S. It is not a center merely in the convex hull of the measured fibers.

The retained product has 2N-1 equal fibers. For an ambient halfspace
through y whose continuous normal has nonzero restriction to the
direction space of K, the scalar thresholds at opposite base positions
are opposite. The audited paired-centroid-tail theorem gives raw mass
at least 2 gamma_q |K| for each pair, and ordinary Grünbaum gives
gamma_q |K| on the middle fiber. Thus every such halfspace has retained
mass at least gamma_q(2N-1)|K|.

If that continuous restriction vanishes, its value is constant on each
retained fiber. The middle fiber and at least one from each opposite
pair are contained in the closed halfspace. Their raw mass is at least
N|K|>=gamma_q(2N-1)|K|, since gamma_q<=1/2. This also handles a normal
transverse to the intrinsic q-space and positive full-fiber boundary
mass. Any containing closed halfspace can be narrowed to one through y,
and every oblique ambient normal is included in one of these cases.

Finally,

    M=2M_r-a+Delta <= (2N-1)a+eta_q a,

so the normalized retained mass fraction is at least

    (3/4)/(1+eta_q/(2N-1)) >= 3/5.

All factors are exact. For n>=1, gamma_q>=gamma_d and 2^(-n)<=1/2
give the claimed OC bound, in fact a strict margin over gamma_q/2.
For n=0, the original body is continuous, q=d, and ordinary Grünbaum
applies separately as stated.

## 6. Counting case, with an independent rank-exclusion argument

If q=0, every nonempty convex fiber is a singleton, a_r=1, and
Delta=M-2M_r+1 is a nonnegative integer. Delta<=1/4 implies Delta=0.
Here one can independently exclude rank>=2 without an Ehrhart formula.
Triangulate the selected N same-parity bases with all of them as
vertices. Its graph is connected and, in rank at least two, contains a
triangle from a full simplex. Thus it has at least N edges. Their
integer midpoints are distinct and outside the original vertex set,
so convexity forces M>=2N and Delta>=1, a contradiction.

Rank zero gives a single source point. In rank one, completeness gives
the same consecutive residue-lattice chain as above. Its 2N-1
intermediate integer positions exhaust S because Delta=0 means exactly
M=2N-1. Convexity and the singleton fibers force their continuous
coordinates to be affine along this chain. Its middle point is in S,
and every closed containing halfspace contains at least N points by
opposite-pair symmetry. The depth is at least N/(2N-1)>1/2. Necessarily
n>=1 in this case under the original positive ambient-dimension and
convex-body hypotheses, so this proves the required OC constant, also
when d=0. No qth-root expression or 0^0 convention is used.

## 7. Dependency and scope conclusion

The proof uses ordinary Brunn--Minkowski (including equality for positive
convex bodies), ordinary Grünbaum, the already audited parity
triangulation inequality, and the already audited paired-centroid-tail
theorem. Its own compactness and lattice/shear steps have been checked
above. It proves a uniform nonempty regime in every intrinsic dimension,
with a deterministic actual center and all closed ambient halfspaces.

The unresolved complementary regime is exactly as stated in the source:
every positive parity class has Delta_r>eta_q a_r. No condition proved in
this audit implies that a global OC counterexample minimum must leave
that complementary regime.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
